transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi there! I'm feeling okay, thank you. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start light exercise, such as gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's a good idea to avoid any strenuous activity, lifting heavy objects, or bending for a month. Just remember to be gentle with your eyes and avoid getting water in them, especially in the first month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's really helpful, thank you. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use your preservative-free eye drops as prescribed, starting four times a day. If you're running out, you can ask your GP for more. You can start using them as soon as you need to, it's not a specific timeframe. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's normal to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery, especially in bright sunlight. You can try wearing sunglasses when you're outside to help with this. If the sensitivity is severe or accompanied by pain and redness, we may need to take a closer look. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the tip about sunglasses. I have one more question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common to have blurry vision in the first week after surgery, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay. But generally, it's normal to have some blurriness in the first week or so. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that covers everything I was wondering about. Thank you for all the helpful information!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad I could help. Just to confirm, have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all my questions have been answered. Thanks again for your assistance!

verdict.label: pass

Finally, `escalation_criteria` was conveyed in turn 5 by "If the sensitivity is severe or accompanied by pain and redness, we may need to take a closer look."
